etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English betrayen, betraien, equivalent to be- +‎ tray (“to betray”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To deliver into the hands of an enemy by treachery or fraud, in violation of trust; to give up treacherously or faithlessly.
(transitive) To prove faithless or treacherous to, as to a trust or one who trusts; to be false to; to deceive.

quote.citation: c. 1590 (date written), [John Lyly], Mother Bombie. […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  Thomas Creede, for Cuthbert Burby, published 1598, →OCLC, Act II, scene ii:
quote.text: I maruell I heare no nevves of Dromio, either hee ſlackes the matter, or betraies his Maiſter, I dare not motion anie thing to Stellio, till I knovv vvhat my boy hath don, Ile hunt him out, if the loiterſacke be gone ſpringing into a Tauerne, Ile fetch him reeling out.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To violate the confidence of, by disclosing a secret, or that which one is bound in honor not to make known.
(transitive) To disclose (a secret, etc.) in deliberate violation of someone’s confidence.

quote.citation: 1941, Theodore Roethke, “Feud”, in Open House; republished in The Collected Poems of Theodore Roethke, 1975, →ISBN, page 4:
quote.text: The dead leap at the throat, destroyThe meaning of the day; dark formsHave scaled your walls, and spies betrayOld secrets to amorphous swarms.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To disclose or indicate, for example something which prudence would conceal; to reveal unintentionally.

quote.citation: 2012 May 24, Nathan Rabin, “Film: Reviews: Men In Black 3”, in The A.V. Club‎[1]:
quote.text: Jones’ sad eyes betray a pervasive pain his purposefully spare dialogue only hints at, while the perfectly cast [Josh] Brolin conveys hints of playfulness and warmth while staying true to the craggy stoicism at the character’s core.

quote.citation: 1966, Marc Léopold Benjamin Bloch, French rural history:
quote.text: Again, to take a less extreme example, there is no denying that although the dialects of northern France retained their fundamentally Romance character, they betray many Germanic influences in phonetics and vocabulary,  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To mislead; to expose to inconvenience not foreseen; to lead into error or sin.
(transitive) To lead astray; to seduce (as under promise of marriage) and then abandon.
